hints: The altitude through $C(1, 7)$ has perpendicular gradient $-2$: $y - 7 = -2(x - 1) \implies 2x + y = 9$.
walkthrough:
The altitude is perpendicular to the chosen base and passes through the opposite vertex.
Calculate the gradient of line $AB$ and write its equation:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{4 - 1}{5 - (-1)} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$y - 1 = \dfrac{1}{2}(x - (-1)) \implies 2(y - 1) = x + 1 \implies x - 2y + 3 = 0$$
$$y = \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{3}{2}$$

Determine the perpendicular gradient and write the altitude equation through $C(1, 7)$:
$$m_{\text{alt}} = -\dfrac{1}{1/2} = -2$$
$$y - 7 = -2(x - 1) \implies y - 7 = -2x + 2 \implies 2x + y = 9$$

hints: Solve the simultaneous equations $x - 2y + 3 = 0$ and $2x + y = 9$.
Calculate base $AB = \sqrt{6^2 + 3^2} = 3\sqrt{5}$ and altitude $CD = \sqrt{(3-1)^2 + (3-7)^2} = 2\sqrt{5}$, then area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(3\sqrt{5})(2\sqrt{5}) = 15$.
walkthrough:
The altitude is perpendicular to the chosen base and passes through the opposite vertex.
Solve the simultaneous equations for the foot of the perpendicular $D$:
$$\text{From altitude: } y = 9 - 2x$$
$$\text{Substitute into line } AB: x - 2(9 - 2x) + 3 = 0$$
$$x - 18 + 4x + 3 = 0 \implies 5x = 15 \implies x = 3$$
$$y = 9 - 2(3) = 3 \implies D(3, 3)$$

Calculate the lengths of base $AB$ and altitude $CD$:
$$AB = \sqrt{(5 - (-1))^2 + (4 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{36 + 9} = \sqrt{45} = 3\sqrt{5}$$
$$CD = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (3 - 7)^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16} = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}$$
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AB \times CD = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3\sqrt{5} \times 2\sqrt{5} = 15$$
